question: Should exec denylist policy have one canonical persisted owner, or remain a union of openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json?
rationale: The PR creates two durable operator policy surfaces with different editing, persistence, and enforcement owners; code review cannot establish that permanent product and security contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use one canonical owner
options.body: Keep denylist policy in exec-approvals.json and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface to avoid competing persisted security policy.

options.title: Approve unioned surfaces
options.body: Retain both surfaces only with explicit acceptance of union semantics, upgrade behavior, UI and CLI ownership, and cross-host enforcement obligations.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause or close the PR if maintaining another cross-host persisted authorization contract is not currently justified.

recommendation.title: Use one canonical owner
recommendation.body: Keep denylist policy in exec-approvals.json and remove the parallel openclaw.json surface to avoid competing persisted security policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent merged authorization work establishes this boundary, and its author is the strongest available owner for the permanent policy contract.
